newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian rights group slams Israel over closure.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian rights group slams Israel over closure.

text.p: A Palestinian human rights group said on Thursday that Israel's closure of the Gaza Strip and the West Bank was causing great human suffering and economic losses to Palestinians.

In a five-page report on the closure's effect on self-ruled Gaza, the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights (PCHR) described as "collective punishment" the travel ban Israel imposed on Palestinians following a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv on March 21.

It said that Israel has turned back 14 Gaza patients who had appointments for treatment in hospitals in Israel and the West Bank between March 23-25. It said that 16 other patients who applied for exit permits were rejected.

Israel says the travel ban was a security measure to prevent more attacks against Israelis. The closure order was imposed after a Palestinian suicide bomber blew himself up at a Tel Aviv cafe last Friday, killing three Israeli women.
The PCHR countered that the closure was unjustified.

"Palestinian patients, including children and elderly men and women struggling against disease whom Israel is preventing from passing through its territory for the purpose of medical treatment could not represent any security threat to Israel," it said.

The report said that Israel has barred 190 Palestinians from leaving the Gaza Strip to travel to Jordan. Palestinians must travel through Israel's territory to get to the West Bank on their way to Jordan.
"Israel's imposing of a blanket closure on the Palestinian lands represents collective punishment against the Palestinian people which is banned by international law," the report said.

Under the 1993 self-rule deal that launched Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, Israel remains in control of all international crossing points between the self-rule areas and the outside world.
The report also said the closure prevented thousands of Palestinian workers from reaching jobs in Israel and suspended most Palestinian exports and imports.
It said that the Palestinian agriculture sector alone was losing more than one million dollars a day as a result of the Israeli closure.
